alerts.title: Red Sea Rerouting Adds Days to Transit Times
alerts.summary: Vessels continue rerouting around the Cape of Good Hope due to Red Sea security risks, significantly extending east-west transit times. Drewry's container rate index held at $4,465/40ft container as of September 3, near its highest level since September 2024.

alerts.title: Transpacific Rates Hit $7,185/FEU as Capacity Tightens
alerts.summary: Shanghai–Los Angeles spot rates climbed to $7,185 per FEU as carriers pulled approximately 20% of transpacific capacity via blank sailings through September. Shippers face omitted calls, port skipping, and last-minute schedule changes as pre-National Day cargo rush and typhoon backlogs converge.

alerts.title: Global Port Congestion Hits 4-Year High
alerts.summary: Over 10% of the global container fleet is waiting at anchorage, with 80% of 454 tracked ports experiencing elevated congestion. Average vessel wait times range from near zero at efficient hubs to over 45 days at the worst-affected ports.

alerts.title: Shanghai, Ningbo, Rotterdam Face Multi-Week Delays
alerts.summary: Severe congestion at Shanghai, Ningbo, Rotterdam, and Antwerp is creating cascading delays across east-west trade lanes, compounded by Typhoon SAUDEL which closed Ningbo for 78 hours this week. Carriers are skipping ports and omitting calls to recover schedules, raising rollover risk for general cargo bookings.

alerts.title: Typhoon SAUDEL Closes Ningbo, Disrupts Asia Schedules
alerts.summary: Typhoon SAUDEL forced the closure of Ningbo port for 78 hours this week and is driving vessel bunching across Asia, with Ningbo now averaging 3.58-day vessel waits and Yokohama at 90-95% yard utilization. The US peak shipping season is extending into September, with the National Retail Federation forecasting 2.31 million TEUs through major US ports in September.

alerts.title: Canada Hits US Steel and Electronics with Tariffs
alerts.summary: Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on US steel, electronics, and other products starting September 8, responding to Washington's 50% levy on $20 billion in Canadian goods. US-Canada trade negotiations remain stalled, with Trump warning of further escalation.

alerts.title: Sep 29 US Regulatory Wave: Canada Ban + Pharma Tariffs
alerts.summary: Two major US trade actions take effect September 29: a prohibition on importation of certain Canadian goods (escalating the US-Canada trade war), and new tariffs on patented pharmaceuticals and active ingredients affecting healthcare importers. Both measures confirmed active as of September 13, adding significant compliance burden for North American supply chains.

alerts.title: US Treasury Broadens Iran Aviation Sanctions
alerts.summary: The US Treasury Department has expanded Iran aviation sanctions, increasing scrutiny of regional support networks and raising compliance risks for MRO companies, freight forwarders, aircraft brokers, and parts suppliers in the UAE, Turkey, Malaysia, and other transit markets. Companies with exposure to these networks face heightened enforcement risk.

alerts.title: Panama Canal Re-Imposes Draft Restrictions in 2026
alerts.summary: The Panama Canal Authority has reintroduced vessel draft restrictions in 2026 as water levels remain below historical norms following the severe 2023-2024 drought. Shippers on trans-Pacific and US East Coast lanes face reduced cargo loads per transit, adding cost and pushing some volume to alternative routes.

alerts.title: Pointe Noire Port Yard Over Capacity, 3+ Day Delays
alerts.summary: Pointe Noire (Republic of the Congo) is experiencing severe yard congestion exceeding 100% utilization, with vessel waiting times reaching 3.4 days and vessel delays of up to five days. The congestion is disrupting cargo flows for West and Central African importers relying on this key gateway.

alerts.title: US Pax Silica Initiative Reshaping Semiconductor Supply
alerts.summary: A new US-led economic cooperation framework called Pax Silica is pulling allied nations into coordinated semiconductor and AI hardware supply chain blocs, accelerating decoupling from Chinese supply networks. Companies dependent on Chinese chip packaging, advanced substrates, or rare earth inputs face growing sourcing disruption risk as the initiative takes hold.

alerts.title: Pre-National Day Cargo Surge to Intensify Sep Congestion
alerts.summary: Shippers are accelerating bookings ahead of China's National Day Golden Week holiday (October 1), compounding congestion caused by typhoon-delayed cargo competing for limited capacity. Carriers have pulled approximately 20% of capacity via blank sailings, pushing FAK bookings into elevated rollover risk through end of September.

alerts.title: China Uses Rare Earth Controls to Extract Tariff Cuts
alerts.summary: Beijing has successfully leveraged export restrictions on rare earth materials as a coercive instrument, pressuring US manufacturers dependent on critical mineral inputs to lobby for tariff reductions. ODI analysis identifies persistent US supply chain vulnerabilities to this form of geoeconomic coercion as a structural risk through 2026 and beyond.

alerts.title: Port Klang Westports Emergency Dredging Sep 7–27
alerts.summary: Emergency maintenance dredging is underway at Malaysia's Port Klang Westports from September 7 to 27, restricting vessel drafts and reducing throughput at one of Southeast Asia's busiest transshipment hubs. September 13 data confirms 1.21-day average vessel waits and 90-95% yard utilization, with schedule adjustments and possible delays expected through end of dredging window.

alerts.title: Semiconductor Country-of-Diffusion Tariffs Add New Risk
alerts.summary: US trade policy has shifted to tariffing semiconductors based on their Country of Diffusion (COD) rather than Country of Origin (COO), adding a significant new compliance layer for importers of chips manufactured or packaged in third countries. Companies with complex semiconductor supply chains sourcing from Asia face increased duty exposure and reclassification risk.

commodityNotes.note: Energy prices surged 24% year-to-date in 2026 to highest level since Russia's Ukraine invasion; Brent crude climbed ~5.7% in August alone with Middle East supply constraints and Strait of Hormuz uncertainty continuing to drive upside risk.
commodityNotes.driver: Middle East conflict, supply constraints, and Strait of Hormuz uncertainty

commodityNotes.note: Copper stabilized near $6.45/lb after a near-5% single-session drop; US tariff reconsideration on refined metals and double-digit output declines at Codelco and Freeport weigh on near-term price direction.
commodityNotes.driver: US tariff uncertainty and major miner double-digit production declines

commodityNotes.note: Steel prices firmer in the US and Europe amid trade barriers and tariff disruptions, while largely unchanged across Asia; North American markets supported by US-Canada trade war and import restrictions.
commodityNotes.driver: US and European tariff barriers and US-Canada trade war disruptions

commodityNotes.note: Natural gas prices elevated as part of broader energy rally; energy index rose 8.8% in August 2026, led by nat gas at +10.1%. Middle East geopolitical risk premium sustains upward pressure.
commodityNotes.driver: Geopolitical risk premium and broader energy price rally

commodityNotes.note: Precious metals surged 8.8% in August 2026, with gold benefiting from geopolitical uncertainty, dollar weakness, and flight-to-safety demand amid Middle East conflict and global trade fragmentation.
commodityNotes.driver: Safe-haven demand from Middle East conflict and global trade fragmentation

commodityNotes.note: Aluminum forecast at $3,800/mt for Q3 2026 and $3,700/mt for Q4, driven by supply disruptions linked to Middle East conflict and potential shifts in Chinese export policy.
commodityNotes.driver: Middle East supply disruptions and Chinese export policy uncertainty

disruptionZones.desc: Ongoing security threats forcing vessels to reroute around Cape of Good Hope, adding 10-14 days to Asia-Europe transit times; Drewry index at $4,465/40ft container near multi-year highs.

Three typhoons in five weeks, including SAUDEL closing Ningbo for 78 hours; Ningbo at 3.58-day waits, Yokohama at 90-95% utilization; Port Klang under emergency dredging Sep 7-27 with 90-95% yard utilization; pre-National Day cargo rush expected to intensify congestion through end of September.

US-Canada trade war escalating: Canada imposed Sep 8 retaliatory tariffs on US steel and electronics; US import prohibition on certain Canadian goods and new pharma tariffs both effective Sep 29; Panama Canal draft restrictions adding further transit cost.
Iran-Gulf state talks in Oman over Strait of Hormuz access introduce uncertainty; ~20% of global oil trade transits this chokepoint daily.
Rotterdam and Antwerp experiencing cascading delays as late-arriving vessels from Asia create uneven cargo surges and operational inefficiencies.
